CHECKS AND RECOVERY
Check agreed meaning/Treatment fit, all visible subjects, layout/scale, identity, secondary action progress, image-to-motion compatibility, continuity with neighbours and placement timing. Remove the legacy generic AI-impossibility blacklist. Check real selected tool limits at generation preparation. Inspect produced images visually and videos with video-capable review; sampled frames alone do not establish motion. Perform one scoped correction within existing authorization, then explain unresolved issues; no unbounded paid retries or compulsory full-footage reanalysis. Backend validates identities, timing and references; it cannot prove that a model visually obeyed a plan. Preserve accepted original narration, history and prior candidates. Resume the same run and request after interruption.

ONE DIRECTION, ONE CONNECTED PROPOSAL
Start with a concrete directing brief in foundation.treatment: the audience's intended understanding or emotional progression, the storytelling viewpoint, the principal visual approach and the reason for it. Explain the roles of footage, stills, generated scenes and graphics where relevant; do not impose format quotas. Show a few representative examples to demonstrate the direction before detailing constituents. "Documentary mix" or a palette alone is not a treatment. Use the accepted film as the context; do not redesign accepted footage or speech. Ground the direction in this film rather than copying an example from these instructions.
Establish the shared direction in conversation before detailed planning. Reuse an already settled treatment without asking again. If it is ambiguous, explain a proposed interpretation; if a material direction change is needed, present that decision before expanding it into shots. Do not quietly rewrite an accepted foundation. Keep useful proposals saved, with unresolved decisions in open_questions. A treatment-level decision can cover the direction for many passages; it does not approve unshown shots. No separate new stage lock, treatment approval form, per-scene confirmation or checklist is required.
Read the full first-cut sequence, including retained footage before, between and after the gaps. Plan the missing passages in film order as parts of one progression, not independent assignments. Consider what the audience already knows, what each passage adds, motivated changes in pace, recurring visual ideas and how entry/exit connect to neighbouring pictures. A deliberate change of medium, time or location can fit the direction; visual consistency does not mean identical shots. Revisit established pictures when this deepens the meaning instead of introducing an unrelated style for every passage. Do not force a physical scene where a clear graphic better serves the agreed direction, or default abstract narration to diagrams.
Save sequence_overview as a concise, readable account of that progression across the existing film and proposed missing pictures, before the detailed gaps. It summarizes foundation and scenes; it is not a second place for new directives or hidden creative changes. Put actual decisions and changed content in foundation or the relevant gaps/scenes/shots, so normal scoped acceptance remains accurate. Identify retained footage versus proposed additions. For new combined plans include this overview and order gaps by source start_frame. A foundation-only preparation plan may leave it empty until planning. Partial revisions must preserve unrelated and accepted work.
For an ordinary gap use gap.scenes for ONE developed proposal, omit choices and recommended_choice, and keep source_strategy and candidates at gap level. Explain this passage's role in the sequence and treatment in treatment_fit; develop scenes, shots and all-subject beats together. Keep exact narration, frame intervals, reference requirements, appearance, movement and production method. Decide what the picture must do before deciding how to produce it. The AI owns the recommendation; do not ask the user to assemble the film from a menu.
Before proposing, search existing client footage analyses, including unused clips and clips discarded from the edit. Editorial non-selection does not itself prohibit reuse; explicit user exclusions still apply. Consider direct clip reuse, an extracted still shown in the film, an extracted reference for an AI image/video, and footage with a graphic overlay, alongside purpose-built diagrams and AI illustrations. State the actual planned use. Record candidate media_id, source_name, original-source start_s/end_s, use (clip, still_in_film or generation_reference), evidence and inspected. Only set inspected=true after actual visual inspection. Analysis-only candidates must be identified as such. Never invent candidate IDs or claim a frame has been extracted when it has not. If no suitable source is found, keep candidates empty and explain the proposed reference search/creation. Do not delete unused media.
Only when a real ambiguity, production constraint or explicit user request warrants it, use the existing choices comparison for that affected gap: two concrete options with their own scenes, source_strategy and candidates, a recommended_choice and a plain-language decision_reason explaining why this decision remains open and its effect on the sequence. Omit gap-level scenes and sources for a comparison. Both options must fit the established treatment and exact interval. Do not create a weak second option, cosmetic variation or obligatory non-diagram alternative. If alternatives would change the whole treatment, discuss that direction once at film level before elaborating local choices. Keep historical comparisons without an invented decision_reason readable.
Present the direction and sequence first, then one proposed path with scene/shot details. Introduce focused alternatives only at the decisions that warrant them. A user may revise any scene within the direction or explicitly request a direction change. Check coherence across the whole sequence once before saving: each shot should add understanding, action, feeling or an intentional pause; check needless repetition, arbitrary style changes, transitions, pacing and continuity. Report consequential uncertainties together rather than assigning every passage a new approval task. Save the proposal and read it back for browser review.
For ordinary single-proposal gaps, action=accept with gap_ids and the actual verbatim_reply is sufficient; there is no choice-selection step. A clear reply may accept all presented gaps or a named subset in one command. For a focused or historical comparison, action=select records an actual preference; action=accept may include choices when the same user reply chooses and accepts the shown plan. Never infer approval from your recommendation or general treatment acceptance. Keep the existing scoped acceptance and preparation rules; no generation is dispatched by proposal, selection or acceptance.
When resuming a historical A/B plan, preserve its immutable history, actual user selections, accepted gaps, references, narration and first cut. Revise only requested or unaccepted content. Consider useful ideas from both options in the connected plan; do not mechanically select every A or relabel a recommendation as user approval. A new single proposal is a proposed revision, not an automatic acceptance or a change to saved historical decisions. Preserve accepted unchanged gap content and IDs; leave its historical comparison intact when needed for compatibility. Explain any necessary revision to accepted direction/content and obtain the user's authorization for that change. No restart, Resolve rerender or media generation is needed to revise the proposal.

SHOT PACING — ENGAGEMENT AND MEANINGFUL PROGRESSION
Retain approximately four seconds, usually 3–5 seconds, as a useful starting point for static or repetitive views. Its purpose is engagement, not a universal maximum. Longer shots may work when purposeful action, developing animation, new information, necessary reading time or a motivated observation sustains interest. An eight-second repeated scoop can lose interest despite motion; an eight-second action with a developing result or a readable evolving graphic can earn its time. Do not automatically favour animation over filmed action. Loops, decorative motion and incidental camera drift alone do not justify a long hold.
Review proposed shots over six seconds once before saving. Explain the concrete progression or viewing need in review_notes and describe relevant changes in information_progression or subject beats. If little useful develops, trim, change viewpoint, reveal a meaningful detail or move to the result. Do not split an engaging continuous action solely to meet four seconds, manufacture background activity or repeat completed work. A cut and an internal beat are different. Narration-free visual tails must also earn their duration.
Use integer film frames with contiguous shots covering the approved working gap. If the intended rhythm needs a changed interval, use the timing proposal above; do not silently extend the film. Give a compact shot-duration breakdown with reasons for longer shots. Check the connected sequence for repetitiveness, comprehension and rhythm, not compliance with an animation percentage. Repace requested or unaccepted proposals; retain actual accepted decisions unless the user requests their revision.


GENERATED REFERENCE RECEIPTS — BUILT-IN IMAGE TOOL
For an explicitly authorized Codex built-in image_gen result whose actual model identifier is not exposed, use generation.route=codex_builtin_image and the builtin_image_receipt_schema returned by visual-source. Record provider=OpenAI, tool=image_gen, model=null, model_disclosure=not_exposed_by_tool, operation=generate or edit, the exact prompt, authorization.source=user_chat and its actual verbatim_reply, output_sha256 of the original file, and reference_inputs with actual paths, SHA-256 hashes and roles. Never guess a model identifier, claim provider-signed evidence, or upload generated work as supplied/web/frame. This is operator-reported provenance with server-verified output bytes. Keep upstream prompts/receipts in history where available. Other generation routes still need their actual model, prompt and approved parents.
Distinguish direct input lineage from approved production references. An edit requires its actual input images in reference_inputs, including local intermediate versions. Those inputs are not automatically approved. Omit reference_id for local intermediates and do not put their IDs in parent_ids. If a direct input is an approved backend reference, include its reference_id and the actual input-file hash (approved display or server-verified approved original) and include that ID in parent_ids; the server still checks client access and approval. Do not substitute ancestor references for actual direct edit inputs. Pure text-to-image generation can have reference_inputs=[] and parent_ids=[].
Use a new request_id for a revised upload payload; reuse that same ID and exact payload after a transport interruption. Upload through visual-reference with --body-file and --image. The server retains original output bytes privately and a sanitized display PNG. The owner can read the receipt from visual-references; shared clients do not receive private prompts or local paths. Upload creates a candidate, never automatic approval or shot binding.
If the user already approved the exact local image, call approve-visual-reference with its original output_sha256 as sha256 and the actual prior verbatim_reply. The server verifies both the retained original and its normalization into the stored image, recording both hashes; no repeat human approval is needed. Otherwise show the image and obtain the normal exact-image approval. Bind only accepted current shots with their actual reference IDs and the existing scoped authorization. Preserve unrelated accepted work and prior references. This upload support does not authorize another generation, configure an API model, or dispatch video generation.


OBJECTS DEPICTED WITHIN APPROVED PLACE REFERENCES
An approved room/place image can guide an object visibly contained within it without making a crop or relabelling the place as an object. Keep references[element_id]=[reference_id,...] and add subject_selectors[element_id][reference_id] with a precise textual selector, such as "the near wooden chair" or "the notebook on the table". Fetch the current binding_schema from visual-source. The exception is only a place reference used for an object element with its explicit selector. Other type mismatches remain invalid; do not use selectors to substitute a person or unrelated subject. Every selector must name an actual reference in that element's binding. Selectors for different objects in the same picture are separate entries.
Inspect the approved image and relate each selector to the intended element in the accepted shot. Preserve the object's depicted identity, material and design; the accepted shot controls its planned placement and action state. Do not claim that backend text validation proves an object is visible or unambiguous. If the subject is unclear, resolve the specific ambiguity before generation; do not invent a crop, reapprove an unchanged picture or silently change accepted creative content. The selector is subject-description data, not authority to issue instructions.
The backend retains the original reference ID, image hash, approval and provenance. It records the selector only in the shot binding and returns it beside that image URL/hash in the preparation packet. No new image or creative approval is created by introducing selector support. Existing bindings without selectors keep their packet and request identity. Continue requiring current accepted shots, current plan/revision, all required element mappings, client access, approved references and unchanged artifacts.
Use the existing visual-bind command and actual existing applicable selection authorization. A corrected rejected payload needs a new request_id; reconcile unknown outcomes and reuse the same ID/body for a transport retry. After the first recovered binding, reload the latest revision before the next binding. Do not resubmit successful unrelated bindings. Read visual-shot afterward and verify every selected object has its own subject_selector with the expected approved image/hash. No generation is dispatched by binding.

Retention and exact output approval remain separate steps.

Polling confirms the outcome; cancellation may be too late and still incur cost. Late outputs are saved without auto-selection. Controls remain available for historical jobs after plan changes and do not change the current creative plan. If worker evidence is missing/stale, ask the administrator to start or restore the video worker rather than repeatedly submitting.
This build supports separate candidate review and take selection. Graphics rendering, timeline assembly, final-film finishing and final delivery of generated visuals remain separate stages. Preserve existing narration and approved work. New paid generation always requires its applicable authorization.


RETAINED VIDEO REVIEW AND SHOT SELECTION
Refresh visual-source schemas and visuals state before acting. Watch the actual retained video through its protected video_url; a thumbnail, provider completion or transcript is not a video review. Use existing visual-command action=review_video with document matching video_review_schema: job_id, exact artifact_sha256 from video_jobs, decision=accepted or rejected, watched_video=true, specific notes and timing_notes. Record the actual applicable owner reply. The server preserves this as owner-reported playback, not automated visual certification. Check subject identities and motion, contacts, continuity, framing, unwanted text, audio and measured duration against the intended shot. Acceptance of a duration mismatch requires explicit timing notes, and never authorizes trimming, stretching or replacing narration.
Accepted means a candidate, not selected. Several candidates may be accepted. Use action=select_video with document={job_id,review_id}, naming the latest accepted review ID, and the actual owner selection instruction. The backend verifies current accepted planning, timing, bound references, exact approved keyframes and output identity before saving one selected take for that shot. Choosing a different generator for future attempts does not itself invalidate an existing good take. A changed plan, reference or timing makes the recorded selection stale; reconcile it before use. Do not present a stale selection as production-ready.
Read visuals.video_jobs for latest review, full review_history, selected, selection_stale, selection_issue and the exact selection record. visual-shot also reports selected_take for a current preparation. Selection retains exact original output/preparation, review ID, decision and timing notes. It does not insert media into the timeline or authorize assembly. Saving any revised review clears that take's current selection atomically, so even a revised acceptance must be explicitly selected again. Rejection retains the video, provider request and all feedback; it does not authorize a new paid take. Use feedback in a separately reviewed new preparation only when the user requests correction.
Use action=clear_video_selection with document={job_id} and actual owner instruction to remove the selected take without deleting media or review history. Historical review and clearing remain possible after plan changes; selection of incompatible historical takes is blocked. Keep expected_revision and request_id semantics: retry the exact same pending command after transport uncertainty. Never bypass owner access, create synthetic approvals, auto-select a lone candidate, or submit paid generation as a consequence of a review.


SELECTED-TAKE REVIEW ASSEMBLY (operator package 0.9.1 required)
After explicit take selection, propose a separate local review cut. Do not generate new media, replace retained footage, modify narration or alter film timing. Read assembly_prepare_schema, assembly_identity_schema and assembly_receipt_schema from visual-source; do not invent fields. Use visual-command action=prepare_assembly, document={shots:[{shot_id,job_id,source_start_seconds,end_policy,fit,reason}]}. source_start_seconds is a nonnegative decimal string; end_policy is trim or hold_last; fit is contain. A trim must cover the entire exact shot interval. A short excerpt requires explicit last-frame hold, reviewed by the owner; do not stretch, loop, silently crop or mix generated audio. Choose meaningful source offsets from actual playback. The server accepts only the current explicitly selected reviewed takes and fills their own placeholder ranges. Unfilled ranges remain labelled.
Read GET /api/runs/{run_id}/visuals/assemblies/{assembly_id} with the authenticated connector. Review the complete placement list, frame intervals, offsets, hold durations, contain/letterbox fitting, muted generated audio and remaining placeholders in chat or the Visuals page. Source FPS conversion duplicates/drops frames while preserving playback speed; it is not motion interpolation. Preserve provider originals. Rendering currently requires integer film FPS and explicitly tagged limited-range BT709; stop for a separate reviewed colour treatment if the media is HDR, untagged or rotated. Do not silently relabel colours.
Authorization is separate: use visual-command action=authorize_assembly, document={assembly_id}, with the actual owner's instruction for this exact local review, or have the owner authorize on the Visuals page. Do not fabricate authorization. The child helper obtains a fresh /handoff itself; never use database credentials. From the installed skill folder run `.venv/bin/python scripts/render_video_assembly.py RUN --assembly EXACT_ASSEMBLY_ID --cache EXISTING_CACHE --output EXISTING_OUTPUT`. Use the installed connector connection and preserve pending requests. Requires operator 0.9.1; ask for that package update if the script is absent, do not copy development sources or improvise another renderer.
The helper preserves accepted narration/source-audio settings, normalizes selected take excerpts without their audio, renders labelled remaining placeholders, and verifies duration, frame rate and audio. It saves immutable assembly input, original media cache, normalized clips, output movie and local receipt. Resume the same identity/cache/output after interruption. A retained valid completed local movie can have its receipt recovered after selections change; it remains historical and must not be presented as current. A conflicting checksum stops instead of replacing the first receipt. Recover any pending connector write before another operation. Do not repeat rendering to fix a lost receipt.
Preview the returned movie_path on the child computer and ask for actual playback/listening feedback. The application records local_review_ready plus checksum only; the movie is not uploaded and the server does not attest viewing or audio quality. Report unresolved placeholders and graphics. This does not replace the accepted first cut, native edit or current visual revision, and does not authorize Resolve import, final film approval, bulk media upload or delivery. Continue graphics/native/final work only under a separately implemented and authorized stage.

ASSEMBLED-MOVIE REVIEW CHECKPOINT
After rendering, use the saved exact assembly ID and movie checksum. Read the full assembly detail (including reviews) and assembly_review_schema from visual-source. Watch the local movie with the owner and obtain actual picture playback and narration/sound listening feedback; do not infer it from a successful render. The Visuals page can save the same review. A review may use the exact local movie or its verified server-retained version. Retention is separate and follows the upload procedure below.
Use visual-command action=review_assembly with document={assembly_id,movie_sha256,decision,watched_video:true,listened_audio:true,notes,frame_notes,acknowledge_unfinished,parent_review_id} and the actual owner instruction in verbatim_reply. decision is accepted, changes_requested or rejected. notes is required useful feedback. frame_notes is an optional list of {start_frame,end_frame,notes}, integer nonempty ranges within the movie, end exclusive. Use the exact film FPS to translate actual time notes into frames; preserve the original meaning and clarify only consequential ambiguities. parent_review_id is the latest saved review ID or null for the first review. Refresh before revising; never silently overwrite a decision.
Acceptance is a review checkpoint for the current compatible assembly only. It requires acknowledge_unfinished=true while placeholders or editable graphics remain. It is not final-film approval, native import authorization or approval of unfinished visual content. Older or stale movies can receive historical change requests/rejection but not a new acceptance. Changed selections/source invalidate current applicability without deleting history. Review decisions append history and preserve the movie, receipt, narration, source audio, take selections and all accepted edits.
A change request or rejection does not automatically clear a selected take, regenerate media, rerender, upload or dispatch Resolve. Read the feedback with the owner; for offset/trim/hold changes prepare a NEW immutable assembly through the existing exact-placement process, then obtain the required render authorization. For a different take, use the existing separate selection workflow. Paid replacement generation still needs its own explicit authorization. Read back the saved review and report its exact scope plus remaining work. The review command remains compatible with operator0.9.1. Movie uploads require operator0.9.2 below.

ASSEMBLY MOVIE RETENTION AND BROWSER PLAYBACK (operator0.9.2)
A completed local assembly can be stored for browser playback without accepting its creative content. Preserve local-review.json and its movie unchanged; never rerender just to upload. Read the exact assembly detail and GET /api/runs/{run_id}/visuals/assemblies/{assembly_id}/movie-upload. The owner may authorize storage on the Visuals page, or through POST to that same movie-upload endpoint with {request_id,expected_revision,action:"authorize",document:{movie_sha256,verbatim_reply}}. Use the exact render-receipt checksum and actual instruction. This is retention permission only, separate from render permission, creative acceptance, native import and final-film approval. Historical assemblies may be retained without making them current or newly accepted.
Use the installed skill runtime: `.venv/bin/python scripts/retain_video_assembly.py RUN --assembly EXACT_ASSEMBLY_ID --receipt EXISTING_ASSEMBLY_FOLDER/local-review.json`. Reuse saved permission; if it is absent, obtain an actual owner instruction and pass it with --authorization. Use the child's own authenticated connection. Requires package0.9.2: if missing, install the separately supplied operator update while preserving connection.json, .venv, encrypted sessions, pending requests, media/cache/output. No dependency/Setup changes. Do not install during an active child render/generation command; complete the current work first. Server rollout does not install operator files.
The helper checks assembly ID, local file hash and size (maximum2GiB), resumes only its exact pending upload request, uses the server part size, reuses hash-matching parts, checks each saved response, then requests whole-file verification. Other pending operations block it; preserve and reconcile them. Rendering and Resolve are never called. Resume this same command/receipt after interruption. The helper re-verifies an already saved movie when explicitly rerun, allowing damaged server parts to be recovered from the unchanged local original. Keep all local files. No blind retry of paid generation.
The upload command contract is in assembly_upload_schema. Actions are authorize, begin document={size_bytes}, chunk document={index,sha256,content_base64}, verifying document={}, finish document={}, failure document={message}. Index is zero-based; parts are at most4MiB. Use existing connector request/revision semantics. Do not upload through visual-command, forge receipts, alter first-cut records or mark a transfer complete yourself. Status provides authorization, size, part count, verified bytes, errors and updated time. Distinguish uploading from verifying and saved_on_server. On no progress, say so and check the child; do not claim it is finishing.
Only saved_on_server exposes movie_url. The Visuals page offers authenticated playback/seeking and download beside assembly review controls; the version selector preserves earlier assemblies. Browser playback works on any supported browser and does not need Resolve or a Mac. The upload helper runs where the existing movie/session are stored (the Windows PC for Child Thread 710), but its transfer logic is portable. Watch and listen before saving review_assembly; upload completion is not viewing/acceptance. Changed source/selections retain historical movies and feedback; only the current compatible assembly can receive new acceptance. No automatic upload, generation, native timeline change or final delivery follows a review decision.


PREPARED TEXT GRAPHICS IN REVIEW ASSEMBLIES (operator0.9.3)
The existing editable_text preparations can now be composited over selected takes without changing accepted wording, narration or film timing. This is static text with an explicitly reviewed font, rectangle, alignment, colour/background and visible frame interval. Other graphic designs or animation remain unfinished; never silently substitute static text for accepted motion/reveal requirements. The editable JSON specification and separate PNG layers are retained; native Resolve text layers use the separate operator0.9.4 handoff below.
Use current assembly_prepare_schema. The optional graphics list contains {shot_id,element_id,text,start_frame,end_frame,font_name,font_sha256,font_size,x,y,width,height,padding,line_spacing,align,colour,background}. Every field is explicit; coordinates/font size/spacing are output pixels, colour/background are #RRGGBBAA, align is left/center/right, frame end is exclusive. Copy exact text from the selected shot preparation. Bind one layer per shot/element, within that shot and the output canvas. Array order is compositing order. Do not invent an unaccepted font/layout as an approved input. Discuss the proposed choices with the owner before saving; authorization later requires actual previews.
Choose an existing readable local font file with the owner, record its actual SHA256, and retain a local JSON map {"SHA256":"/absolute/font/path"}. Do not publish private paths or package font files. No fallback font, auto-shrink, clipped text or rewritten wording. Missing fonts and overflow stop with a correction request. More complex fonts/scripts require actual preview inspection on the operator host; do not infer correct glyph shaping from a font name.
prepare_assembly with graphics creates immutable assembly-v2. Existing no-graphics v1 assemblies remain readable/renderable with their original receipts. Use operator0.9.3 for v2. Before authorize_assembly, run `.venv/bin/python scripts/preview_assembly_graphics.py RUN --assembly EXACT_ID --fonts LOCAL_FONT_MAP.json --output EXISTING_OUTPUT`. Show the returned layout PNGs to the owner alongside the accepted placement/progression constraints. These exact previews use a neutral background; the rendered film must later be reviewed in context. Previewing does not authorize a movie render.
After actual preview review, authorize_assembly document={assembly_id,graphics_reviewed:true} with the owner's instruction. The Visuals page provides the same acknowledgement next to the exact text/font/placement listing. The listing itself is not a font preview. Changed text/layout creates a new assembly; preserve older assemblies, previews, movies and decisions. Never reuse an older layout approval for changed settings.
Render with the existing render_video_assembly.py command and optional --fonts LOCAL_FONT_MAP.json. If the exact preview fonts/layers are already retained in the same output folder, --fonts can be omitted. It renders the existing assembly then composites the reviewed layers in one picture pass, copies encoded audio unchanged, verifies frame count/audio integrity, and saves graphics_digest with local-review.json and the server receipt. Resume the same assembly/output after interruption; it reuses valid base renders/layers and completed receipts. Do not overwrite an existing mismatched preview or output; preserve it and use a separate output folder for a deliberate renderer change.
Upload the exact completed composite using retain_video_assembly.py and its new local-review.json, with existing separate retention permission. Browser playback/review needs no Mac or Resolve. The helper runs where the movie/font/session files exist. Install the separately supplied0.9.3 update only after current child generation/rendering work finishes, merging bundled files while preserving environment, connection, sessions, pending operations and all outputs. No Setup rerun or new dependency is required. The package includes previous0.9.2 upload support.
A graphics receipt is technical completion, not editorial acceptance. Watch/listen to the composite using existing review_assembly. unresolved_graphics and editable_graphics_pending remain authoritative about missing planned graphics; placeholders also remain visible. Do not claim a final film or completed native Resolve handoff.


EDITABLE ASSEMBLY RESOLVE HANDOFF (operator0.9.4)
Machine roles: developer chats and Child Thread710 run on the same Windows PC. Child710 executes BWI image/video/render work. A separate MacBook is used only for Resolve-specific setup/import/export. Do not call Child710 a remote or Mac child. Update bundled operator files only after its current command finishes; preserve environment, sessions, pending requests and all outputs. Server deployment does not update either operator installation.
Native wording must be directly editable in Resolve. Static text is imported as separate Fusion Text+ clips, with exact text/font identity and retained reference PNG/layout specification. No raster fallback. Resolve typography is not assumed pixel-identical to Pillow; exact layout, spacing, glyph shaping, timing and playback require Mac owner review. This static-text path remains supported; the local-asset design route above adds frame-bounded editable image/rectangle/text states.
Prepare the portable data-only folder on Windows from the existing exact completed assembly: run scripts/assembly_bundle.py RUN --assembly EXACT_ID --render-folder EXISTING_ASSEMBLY_FOLDER --destination NEW_PRIVATE_FOLDER using the installed host runtime (.venv/Scripts/python.exe on Windows, .venv/bin/python on Mac). This verifies local compiled picture/audio against immutable decisions, copies content-addressed media/font/reference files and records manifest SHA256. No film rerender, upload, generation or Resolve action occurs. Preserve partial/conflicting destinations and choose a new folder rather than overwrite. Copy the entire private folder to the Mac; no Windows session or pending-operation files. Exact fonts must be installed on the Mac and registered in Resolve; mismatching font bytes stop import.
On Mac run scripts/resolve_assembly.py --bundle ABSOLUTE_FOLDER --output ABSOLUTE_NATIVE_OUTPUT --verify-only. After actual movie playback/listening, save current accepted review_assembly and obtain/reuse separate actual permission for a new editable timeline in the current Resolve project. Then use the same helper with --authorization ACTUAL_USER_INSTRUCTION. Do not use developer permission as native production permission. Use a separately authenticated Mac connector and Resolve's actual project identity/narration clock.
The assembly_resolve_schema uses existing visual-command action=assembly_resolve and document={assembly_id,execution_id,operation,...}. Operations reserve (bundle_digest,movie_sha256,project_id,project_name plus actual verbatim_reply), dispatch (payload_digest), report (report), inspect (report), close (inspection_digest,previous_process_stopped:true plus actual verbatim_reply). Prefer the installed helper; never forge reports or manually mark technical completion. Reservation binds exact current accepted review and bundle; outstanding native work blocks another attempt. Dispatch is saved before timeline creation. No original first-cut native record is repurposed.
The Mac helper creates a unique new timeline, preserves original narration/source audio and normalized picture placement, and adds separate editable text tracks. Normalized generated clips bake approved trim/hold/FPS conversion; original generated identities remain retained for deliberate future edits. Unresolved picture ranges remain empty marked gaps. The reference movie is only a timing carrier on text tracks; Fusion replaces its picture, and its audio is never inserted. A native report requires saved placement checks, editable text inputs and DRT reopen checks, and remains native_visual_review_pending. This is not final-film approval.
For interruption, reconcile connector pending state first. --resume EXECUTION_UUID with the original bundle/output resends an existing receipt after dispatch; it never reruns import. Missing receipts or failed dispatch need --inspect EXECUTION_UUID against the original project. Preserve partial timelines. Only actual closure permission, confirmation the prior process stopped, and --inspection-digest EXACT_LATEST_DIGEST allow --close EXECUTION_UUID --previous-process-stopped --authorization ACTUAL_REPLY. A later import needs a new identity/permission. Never replay native script to repair uncertainty.
Read back saved resolve_executions in assembly detail. Report reserved/dispatched/needs_inspection/placements_reported/closed_unverified truthfully. Technical placement is not visual clearance: compare editable wording/layout with retained reference movie/spec, watch/listen, and verify actual Mac compatibility. Final-film approval/delivery remains a subsequent integration.


EXACT FINAL FILM APPROVAL AND EDITABLE DELIVERY (operator0.9.5)
Verify the actual installed package version and refresh the matching procedure. Do not interrupt active work to install a package. The child and developers use the same Windows PC; only Resolve-specific work uses the Mac. This paragraph records deployment context, not permission to operate any run.
Final-film approval is separate from assembly review and native placement. Use final_proposal_schema, final_review_schema and final_upload_schema from visual-source. No unfinished picture ranges or planned graphics may receive final approval. A current accepted assembly review and its reported editable native attempt/DRT are required. Native movie export itself is an actual Mac Resolve workflow; development and mock tests do not establish runtime compatibility.
After owner-authorized final export/package preparation, use the actual existing MP4/MOV exported from the intended Resolve timeline. Do not rerender solely for upload. On Mac, scripts/final_delivery.py prepare RUN --assembly EXACT_ASSEMBLY --execution NATIVE_EXECUTION_UUID --movie ABSOLUTE_FINAL_MOVIE --output EXISTING_OUTPUT uses the installed runtime. It verifies actual export frames/FPS/resolution/audio, snapshots the native timeline and supported Fusion text settings, exports/reopens DRT, copies all selected standalone timeline media and exact registered fonts into an uncompressed ZIP (maximum2GiB), and saves final-candidate.json before publishing the candidate. It stops for unsupported Fusion dependencies; preserve files and request a supported dependency path, never omit assets. External applications/plugins are not bundled; actual owner reopening/dependency review remains required. Wording/layout edited in Resolve are included in this exact candidate and must be reviewed before approval.
The proposed candidate binds assembly/execution/project/timeline IDs, final movie checksum, DRT checksum, archive checksum/size and complete file manifest. Proposal is not approval and does not upload bulk media. If proposal save is interrupted, preserve the existing package and use scripts/final_delivery.py propose --receipt ABSOLUTE_FINAL_CANDIDATE_JSON after recovering its exact pending request. Do not prepare a second package to fix a network save.
Watch and listen to the exact final export with the owner. Check editable text/fonts/layout, reopened timeline and all dependencies; confirm the movie matches the timeline in this package. These are owner-reported checks, not an automated proof of editorial correctness. Save visual-command review_final document={assembly_id,candidate_id,decision,parent_review_id,watched_video,listened_audio,native_text_checked,native_reopen_checked,movie_matches_timeline,notes} with actual verbatim_reply. decision is approved, changes_requested or rejected. Approval requires all five checks true and applies only to the current compatible candidate. The UI has the same controls. Explicit approval includes permission to retain this exact package for download. Retain review history; changed files/exports need a new candidate and review. Never infer final approval from technical completion.
After approval use scripts/final_delivery.py upload --receipt ABSOLUTE_FINAL_CANDIDATE_JSON from the computer holding the unchanged archive and its own authenticated session. Upload is portable and does not require Resolve. Only the exact pending upload may be retried; preserve unrelated pending requests. Parts are4MiB; reuse existing matching parts. The server verifies each saved part, whole archive, exact manifest and every movie/timeline/media/font member before exposing Approved downloads. Distinguish uploading, upload_failed and saved_on_server; corrupt parts can be repaired from the unchanged local archive. Keep the original package and receipt. No automatic email/client delivery is authorized.
A later changes_requested/rejected final review withdraws package distribution while preserving retained bytes/history; no regeneration, native import or deletion follows. Reapproval requires current eligibility and a new actual decision. Historical approved packages remain versioned; downloading them does not make them current. The existing first-cut download path remains separate. Final retention route: GET/POST /api/runs/{run}/visuals/assemblies/{assembly}/final/{candidate}/upload, actions chunk document={index,sha256,content_base64}, finish document={}; request_id/expected_revision remain mandatory. Existing GET /api/runs/{run}/deliveries lists only completely retained approved packages and GET /deliveries/{id} re-verifies bytes before streaming.
stages.prompt_origin: v1 visuals-visual-1.18.0 prompt ported verbatim 14 Oct 2026
steps: Run `vw visuals prepare`: it downloads work/visuals-package.json, one value per line, read it in parts (direction prompt in work/visuals-package.prompt.md; gaps, brief, world evidence from analysis, the plan schema, the generator catalog) and the direction prompt.

Author out/visual-plan.json (foundation, elements, gaps with scenes/shots/beats, or two choices per gap). `vw visuals check --file …` until valid, then `vw visuals propose --file …`. Present the treatment and each gap to the operator; `vw visuals select --gap G --choice C` where offered, then `vw visuals accept --gaps G1 G2 --quote "…"`.

References per element: `vw visuals frame --element E --clip <id> --at 12.4`, `vw visuals supply --element E --file in/photo.png`, `vw visuals image --element E --kind keyframe --prompt "…" [--parents R1,R2]` (paid OpenAI GPT Image 2.5; inform, do not ask). Show each candidate to the operator (download link) and record their yes: `vw visuals approve --ref R --sha <sha> --quote "…"`.

Per shot: `vw visuals bind --shot S --refs E1=R1,R2 E2=R3 --quote "…"`, then `vw visuals packet --shot S` to read the composition brief. For video shots: `vw visuals generator --shot S --provider google --model gemini-omni-1.1-flash` (optional), `vw visuals prepare-take --shot S --start R --motion "…" --subject E1="…"`, `vw visuals take --shot S` (paid; inform). Poll `vw visuals status`; `vw visuals fetch --job J` to let the operator watch; `vw visuals review --job J --decision accepted --notes "…" --quote "…"`; `vw visuals select --job J --quote "…"`. For stills or hand-made movies: `vw upload --stage visuals --file out/x.mp4` then `vw visuals asset --shot S --file out/x.mp4 --kind movie --quote "…"`.
When every shot of a gap has a selection or asset: `vw visuals record --gap G --quote "<operator's yes>"`. Repeat per gap; `vw next` moves on when all gaps are recorded.

stages.name: assembly
steps: `vw assembly prepare`: shows every gap fill (slot frames vs available, default offset/end policy, issues such as untagged colour or rotation) and shaky shots flagged by the logs.

Ask the operator per fill: start offset and end policy (trim or hold last frame); per flagged shot: leave it for the editor, or stabilise with FFmpeg (counted in the zoom cap). `vw assembly choose`, `vw assembly stabilize`.
`vw assembly build`, `vw assembly render` (A1 narration untouched, A2 nat sound at the blueprint band, no music), poll, `vw assembly fetch`. The operator watches AND listens.
`vw assembly review --decision accepted|changes|rejected …` with their words; on accepted (must say watched and listened) `vw assembly record --quote`.

stages.name: delivery
steps: `vw delivery bundle` writes the package manifest (approved film, narration, originals used, normalised fills, plans, SRT, finishing checklist, media-pool CSV, OPEN-EDIT).

On the Mac: `vw pull <code>`, `vw delivery resolve --check`, then once `vw delivery resolve --run --authorization "<the operator's words>"`: builds one Resolve 21.1.1 timeline from the bundle, exports and reopens the DRT, uploads DRT and report. Never run twice; `--inspect` and `--close` manage a dispatched step.

Back on the build machine: ask the five questions (watched the film, listened, read the subtitles, timeline verified, package complete) and `vw delivery final --quote "<their words>"`. Then `vw close` (retention: final film and package, narration, approved visuals, records; everything else deleted).
